newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Roth urges flexibility in tax talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Roth urges flexibility in tax talks.

text.p: Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth on Monday urged all parties in ongoing tax negotiations to show flexibility.
The Delaware Republican said in a statement that he continued to "strongly urge that all parties involved must be flexible."
Congressional tax negotiators met with administration officials over the weekend in an effort to move toward compromise on a tax cut bill that can pass Congress and be signed by the president.
Roth said he had shown flexibility by offering to scale back his main priority in the tax bill of expanding Individual Retirement Accounts.

"If we are to come up with a tax relief bill that can pass the House and Senate and be signed by President Clinton, I would hope that others would be willing to show the same kind of flexibility," he said.
